commitments.summary: The Department of Correction, with the Law Department, must regularly update the Mayor on additional emergency suspensions that can be lapsed to comply with the action plan and applicable laws.

commitments.summary: The first of five PIT Crews will operationalize the Click-to-Cancel Rule, building the supporting websites and portals, by this fall.

commitments.quote: Starting in October, we're going to have a rule where you have to make it as easy to cancel as it is to sign up.
commitments.summary: Starting in October, the city's Click-to-Cancel rule takes effect, requiring cancellation to be as easy as sign-up, with fines over $500 per violation.

commitments.quote: We are going to present $1.7 billion in savings at the executive budget, and we are going to do so in a manner that both finds efficiencies and savings and does not compromise city services.

commitments.quote: And so, with the 1,000 additional seats that we are bringing forward across the city, that is going to help us finally bridge that gap and make it easier to find free child care closer to home when your child is three years old.
commitments.summary: The city will bring forward 1,000 additional 3-K seats across the city.

commitments.quote: Under the City Administrative Procedures Act (CAPA), New Yorkers will have 30 days to submit comments, including at a public hearing. After the comment period, DCWP will review feedback before finalizing the rule.

commitments.quote: Beginning in June, we will start offering free guided tours led by DCAS staff. Visitors will be able to reserve tickets online.
commitments.summary: DCAS will begin free guided public tours of the Dinkins Municipal Building rooftop and cupola in June, with online ticket reservations.

commitments.quote: We're also going to invest $6 million to improve this building as we repaint the cupola, repair the rotunda, add glass barriers and restore this one-of-a-kind civic space to a landmark befitting Mayor Dinkins name.
commitments.summary: The city will invest $6 million to repaint the cupola, repair the rotunda and add glass barriers at the Dinkins Municipal Building.

commitments.quote: That signage is going to be rolling out today and tomorrow.
commitments.summary: The city, with NYCEM, will add signage outside warming units identifying them, rolling out by February 3.

commitments.quote: Yesterday, Mayor Mamdani announced that the City had doubled those efforts, adding 2,000 3-K seats across all five boroughs and confirming that the City’s ninth new child care center will open this fall in Columbia Waterfront.
commitments.summary: The city will open its ninth new child care center in Columbia Waterfront this fall.

commitments.quote: That work will continue through the Mamdani administration’s commitment to baseline $5 million annually for outreach and engagement.

commitments.quote: After years of stagnation, this is the first of six new recreation centers currently under development by New York City Parks.
commitments.summary: NYC Parks is developing five more new recreation centers following the Shirley Chisholm center; no completion date given.

commitments.quote: This center will remain low-cost to all New Yorkers and free to anyone under the age of 24.
commitments.summary: The Shirley Chisholm Recreation Center will stay low-cost for all New Yorkers and free for anyone under 24.

commitments.quote: Beginning this fall, we will expand our existing specialized education programs — Nest, Horizon, AIMS, Path, and ACES — into Pre-K for the very first time, so that students with autism and developmental delays can be served closer to home alongside their peers.
commitments.summary: The city will expand the Nest, Horizon, AIMS, Path and ACES specialized education programs into Pre-K starting this fall.

commitments.quote: And we will bring new preschool specialized education programs to families in every single borough, at 26 schools across 14 districts.
commitments.summary: The city will open new preschool specialized education programs at 26 schools across 14 districts, in every borough.

commitments.quote: That means 35 additional new staff members, including psychologists, social workers, speech evaluators and occupational therapists to build out 10 additional preschool evaluation teams that will significantly reduce IEP evaluation wait times.
commitments.summary: The city will hire 35 additional staff to build 10 more preschool evaluation teams to cut IEP evaluation wait times.

commitments.quote: It means 20 new administrators and community coordinators on our Committee of Preschool Special Education and 100 new New York City Public School staff members who will support families as they navigate the IEP process.
commitments.summary: The city will hire 20 administrators and coordinators for the Committee of Preschool Special Education and 100 new school staff to support families through IEPs.

commitments.quote: And it means building on the successful pilot of our special education itinerant teacher program by hiring an additional 29 therapists and specialists to help preschoolers with IEPs learn alongside their peers.
commitments.summary: The city will hire 29 additional therapists and specialists for the special education itinerant teacher program for preschoolers with IEPs.

commitments.quote: So, the City Council will have these contracts in the coming weeks and we know that long-standing New York City Public School posture has been that when sharing contracts with an external body that they would go through a vendor review and a redaction process.
commitments.summary: The Department of Education will give the City Council the requested contracts in the coming weeks, with expedited review and non-redacted portions shared.

commitments.quote: In addition, for the first time in city history, we're going to be dispatching city workers to check in on seniors that anyone are concerned about and to see if they need any assistance with this temperature, given what the impacts of this heat often have been.
commitments.summary: The city will dispatch city workers to check on seniors that people are concerned about during the heat wave.

commitments.summary: The administration will not reopen the former Medicare Advantage program for city retirees.
